audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers give Trundle all seven stages while the lane sits at 51.10% over 456 games — the largest sample in my slice — and four of the seven whys describe the stage as even or lost: whys[2] "the window is even", whys[3] "a genuine coin-flip", whys[5] "the advantage is real but fragile", whys[6] "Trundle's window to close the game has passed".
audit.why: A clean sweep printed over a 51% lane is a chart nobody can act on. The paragraphs already say where the stages actually sit, and the kit agrees: Trundle owns levels 1 and 2 because Sweeping Blade cannot be re-cast on the same target for a few seconds, and owns level 6 because Subjugate arrives before Yasuo's crit items do.
audit.corrected: Trundle at levels 1, 2 and 6; Skill at level 3, levels 4-5 and first item; Yasuo at two-plus items.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole page is built on outlasting Last Breath — wants.you[2] "Track Last Breath cooldown — only commit your all-in when it is down", breakdown.mid "when it is up, give nothing", dosFull[0].d "While down, you win" — and no field gives its cooldown. spikes[3] says his "crit burst bypasses the resistance stack Subjugate builds" without saying how.
audit.why: Last Breath is 70/50/30 seconds. Against Subjugate's 120/100/80 it is up roughly twice as often, so "only fight when his ultimate is down" is a plan that quietly stops existing around level 11. And the bypass is a real, named mechanic rather than a vague one: Riot's text says that for a moderate time after Last Breath, Yasuo's critical strikes gain significant Bonus Armor Penetration — which is precisely why the armour Subjugate lends you evaporates in the late game.
audit.corrected: Last Breath 70/50/30s against Subjugate's 120/100/80. After it lands, his crits carry bonus armour penetration for a while — that is the late-game bypass.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page states Last Breath's casting condition. spikes[1] even says to "run him down before Last Breath lands", as though it were a spell he can throw at any moment.
audit.why: Last Breath blinks to an AIRBORNE enemy champion. The only airborne it gets in a 1v1 is Yasuo's own whirlwind — Steel Tempest at two stacks of Gathering Storm. So the entire matchup reduces to one instruction: sidestep the third Steel Tempest. Deny the knockup and a 70-second ultimate has nothing to jump to, which is a far more useful rule than counting a cooldown that halves as it ranks.
audit.corrected: Last Breath needs an airborne target. Two Steel Tempest stacks make the whirlwind; sidestep it and his ultimate has no entry.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] says Yasuo should "Windwall your Pillar approach or knock-up animation to deny the terrain cutoff and escape the W zone".
audit.why: Wind Wall blocks enemy projectiles for 4 seconds. Every ability in Trundle's kit is either point-and-click or ground-placed — Chomp is a 300-range targeted bite, Frozen Domain and Pillar of Ice are ground-targeted, Subjugate is a 650-range targeted cast, and none of them carries a projectile flag in the kit library. So a Wind Wall thrown at a Trundle in lane is 25 seconds of his most valuable cooldown spent on his own team's poke, and the correct reading is that the cast is a window to step in, not a reason to back off.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall (25s at rank 1, 4 seconds) is aimed at projectiles — treat one thrown in lane as free aggression.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sweeping Blade is called "his Steel Tempest dashes" in `early` and its restriction is nowhere on the page. Steel Tempest itself is never identified as an attack.
audit.why: Riot's text says Sweeping Blade cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds — so once Yasuo dashes through Trundle, his only way back in is through a minion. That makes denying him the wave a mobility answer, not just a damage one, and it is the reason a Pillar of Ice cutting him off from the minions is worth more than one placed behind him. Steel Tempest is also "treated as a basic attack and scales with all the same things", which means Chomp's Attack Damage sap cuts his Q as well as his autos.
audit.corrected: Sweeping Blade cannot re-target the same enemy for a few seconds. Steel Tempest is treated as a basic attack, so the AD sap cuts it too.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] says Chomp "slows his attack speed". spikes[1] and whys[4] describe Subjugate as draining "a chunk of Yasuo's armor".
audit.why: Chomp saps Attack Damage and slows movement. Subjugate takes 40% of both resistances and, more importantly against a champion with Yasuo's health bar, a fifth of his maximum health as damage plus the same again as healing for Trundle — the part of the ultimate that actually decides the level-6 duel here.
audit.corrected: Chomp: AD sap, movement slow. Subjugate: 40% of resists plus a fifth of max health, healing the same.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flags one probable wrong ability name ("Last Breath's" in `mid`, a false positive). The real point-6 problem is that breakdown.cooldowns names two abilities and gives neither a number.
audit.why: Last Breath 70/50/30s, Wind Wall 25/23/21/19/17s, Steel Tempest a flat 4s, Sweeping Blade under a second, against Chomp's flat 3.5s and Pillar of Ice's 21s. The one worth writing down is Wind Wall: at 25 seconds it is his longest laning cooldown, and against a kit with no projectiles it is the cheapest thing in the matchup to bait.
audit.corrected: Figures added to breakdown.cooldowns, phases[2], phases[4], report[5], dosFull[0], mid, late and three whys.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] buys Executioner's Calling on the first back "— cuts his healing".
audit.why: No Yasuo ability carries a heal flag and _missing-interactions.json raises no needs-antiheal for this matchup. His sustain is item-borne — Immortal Shieldbow's lifesteal, Bloodthirster later — so the buy is right eventually and wrong at 800 gold on the first back, where a Trinity Force component does more for the window Trundle actually owns.
audit.corrected: Executioner's Calling once he has lifesteal, not on the first back by default.

audit.why: The packet's only suspectName, "Last Breath's" in `mid`, is a possessive and a false positive. Worth recording separately: Yasuo's Q carries both a dash and a projectile flag in the kit library — the dash is a tooltip artefact of the E-into-Q circle interaction and I did not write it as a dash anywhere.

edits.before: Level 1 is Trundle's most reliable window in this lane. Open Q and bite Yasuo every time he steps up to last-hit — the AD steal immediately reduces how hard he hits back, and King's Tribute healing from minion deaths means his return autos heal a chunk of what he dealt. Do not chase past the minion wave or he turns with the minion damage backing him; just take the bite-and-out pattern and repeat. At level 2 drop Frozen Domain at your feet the moment he commits — the movement speed lets you stick to him through his Steel Tempest dashes and the attack speed closes the exchange faster than he expects.
edits.after: Level 1 is Trundle's most reliable window in this lane. Open Q and bite Yasuo every time he steps up to last-hit — the AD sap immediately cuts how hard he hits back, and because Steel Tempest is treated as a basic attack it lands on his Q too. King's Tribute heals you off the minions dying beside you. Do not chase past the wave or he turns with the minion damage behind him; bite and leave, then repeat. At level 2 drop Frozen Domain at your feet the moment he commits — Sweeping Blade cannot be re-cast on you for a few seconds, so his only way back in is through a minion.

edits.before: The mid window depends entirely on Last Breath's cooldown. When it is down Trundle runs his full pattern: W at feet, Q Chomp to bite AD, Pillar behind Yasuo to cut off retreat, weave autos in the W zone. When it is up, give nothing — Yasuo only wins this lane by landing a knockup into Last Breath because that is the only time his burst outraces Chomp healing and W sustain. At level 6 lead with Subjugate before the second auto lands so the drained armor counts for every hit in the fight; Yasuo loses the 1v1 almost regardless of shield state when Trundle is inside his W and R is online.
edits.after: The mid window depends on Last Breath, but not the way this lane's reputation says: it is 70 seconds at rank 1 and 30 at rank 3, so waiting it out stops being a plan. Play the condition instead — Last Breath blinks to an AIRBORNE champion, so if the two-stack Steel Tempest whirlwind never lands, the ultimate has nothing to jump to. Run the pattern while sidestepping that third Q: W at your feet, Chomp to sap his AD, Pillar of Ice cutting him off from the wave, autos in the zone. At 6, open with Subjugate so the 40% steal and the max-health hit cover the whole fight.

edits.before: Past two items the lane flips. Yasuo's crit spikes with Immortal Shieldbow and Infinity Edge let him one-shot-pattern with Last Breath into a team knockup, and the resistance Subjugate drains is far less meaningful against an AD carry than against a tank. Trundle is still a functional duelist and can win isolated 1v1s with R up, but the macro shifts: look for objective fights where Subjugate can drain a tanky frontliner in 5v5 rather than trying to catch Yasuo alone at full items. If the lane was snowballed early, force Yasuo into side-lane duels with Pillar cutoffs; if it was even, respect the late-game ceiling and play toward your team's tankier members as R targets.
edits.after: Past two items the lane flips. Yasuo's crit spikes with Immortal Shieldbow and Infinity Edge, and for a while after Last Breath lands his critical strikes carry significant bonus armour penetration — the specific reason the resistances Subjugate lends you stop counting. Trundle is still a functional duelist and wins isolated 1v1s with R up, but the macro shifts: look for objective fights where Subjugate takes a fifth of a tanky frontliner's health rather than chasing Yasuo alone. If the lane was snowballed early, force him into side-lane duels with Pillar of Ice cutoffs; if it was even, respect the ceiling and pick the tankier R target instead.

notes: Best finding here is the Wind Wall inversion. wants.foe[0] tells Yasuo to Wind Wall Trundle's Pillar approach; Wind Wall stops projectiles and no ability in Trundle's kit carries a projectile flag — Chomp is a 300-range targeted bite, W and E are ground-placed and Subjugate is a targeted cast — so a Wind Wall spent in this lane is 25 seconds of his best cooldown gone. This is the mirror image of the Azir case in the calibration notes: there the Wind Wall interaction was missing; here one was invented. Second: the page's entire plan is 'only fight when Last Breath is down', and Last Breath is 70/50/30s against Subjugate's 120/100/80 — he gets his back roughly twice as often, so the real gate is the airborne condition, not the timer. Third: Last Breath granting bonus armour penetration on crits afterwards is the named mechanic behind the vague 'bypasses the resistance stack' line, and it is in Riot's own text.
